parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation ever, no documented police sweeps, facility bans, or targeting of gender-nonconforming people; no visitor-facing border or document exposure is documented. The negatives are mostly resident-facing (unimplemented legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination law) which per the rubric are climate signals, not traveller exposures. Real traveller-facing concerns: routine healthcare discrimination toward trans women and stigma-driven violence risk (2024 UN feature, resident-focused but reaches any ill or injured visitor), absent protections meaning harassment has thin recourse, prison housing unresolved if detained, and a documented 2025 government clampdown (Pride cancellations, vague penal-code arrests, NGO surveillance) signalling a narrowing civic space. Social attitudes are comparatively tolerant. This sits near the 0.65 tier: no organised targeting or universal exposure, but real friction, weak recourse, and an adverse political trajectory, rather than documented protective machinery.
